body: Little King's Story is Cing and Town Factory's Wii adventure combining real-time strategy with the management of a growing kingdom. Corobo, a timid boy who discovers a mysterious crown, gains the ability to command people and becomes ruler of Alpoko. Leading citizens into the surrounding countryside provides treasure and opportunities to expand the settlement. Their different occupations turn the population into both a community and the means of exploring beyond it. The kingdom begins modestly, giving each new building and newly trained follower a visible place in its development.

Corobo gathers followers and directs individuals toward work, obstacles or enemies. A farmer can dig effectively but is poorly suited to a fight, while a soldier's strengths do not solve every problem in the landscape. Training facilities change citizens' occupations, so preparing an expedition involves deciding what kinds of help the next route requires. The group remains physically present around its king, making an order an action performed by a particular person. Success depends on using the population's different abilities rather than treating every follower as an interchangeable unit.

Treasure and successful expeditions finance new buildings, while requests placed in the town's suggestion box provide additional work for Corobo. The settlement also marks major events with celebrations that can interrupt the usual routine of issuing commands. These details give the people a role beyond serving as a resource for the next campaign. Returning home allows the player to see the effects of expansion, adjust the workforce and hear another complaint. The adventure's larger ambitions grow from a place whose daily activity becomes increasingly familiar as its borders spread.
